title: IRR: two diverging witnesses, candidate scores, and a retracted identification
status_plain: IRR has no production pass count anywhere in OxFunc. Its catalogue row publishes two diverging witnesses at 80 and 14,096 ULP and nothing else. What does exist is a sequence of candidate-schedule scores from the W109 solver lane -- 104 of 177, 112 of 177, 129 of 229, 132 of 229 -- every one of them a simulator or mask fit racing against the corpora it was designed from, and every one of them in-sample by construction. The lane's own field diary then records that an earlier IRR identification was an over-fit of the small-error plateau, which is the most important sentence about IRR in the repository. IRR's absence of a count is not an extraction gap; it is the state of the evidence.

retractions.withdrawn_claim: the Act IV IRR identification: "one-step FD, h = 1e-6·v, three-digit match"
retractions.superseded_by: It was an over-fit of the small-error plateau. A single finite-difference step's error ratio must grow about 25 times across the ladder while the data's ratio moves 4.5 per cent.

open_question: Exact tolerance, cap and order remain open. The catalogue row is M1: no fix has landed and IRR's solver is not identified.
reader_warning: IRR has no production pass count. Every fraction in this record scores a candidate simulator or mask fit on a corpus built to fit it, across three different denominators, and one earlier identification in this same lane was retracted as an over-fit. IRR must never inherit a figure from a PRICE record or from any sibling solver.
